# Security Checklist: User Password Management

**Purpose**: Review the quality of the password-management requirements for completeness, clarity, consistency, and testability.
**Created**: 2026-10-08
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are all required account lifecycle behaviors documented for account creation, sign-in, and password change, including both success and failure states? [Completeness, Spec §User Story 1-3]
- [ ] CHK002 Are the credential validation rules for blank values, duplicate usernames, offensive entries, and invalid current-password flows fully specified? [Completeness, Spec §Edge Cases, Spec §FR-002 to FR-013]
- [ ] CHK003 Are the security controls for password reuse, password history, rate limiting, and session invalidation explicitly documented as part of the requirement set? [Completeness, Spec §FR-014 to FR-024]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK004 Is the password policy written with measurable criteria for length, case sensitivity, numeric content, and special-character requirements? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK005 Is the offensive-word rule precise enough to remove ambiguity about what counts as prohibited text and how it is enforced? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK006 Are the user-visible error outcomes for wrong current password, duplicate username, same-password change, and missing current password clearly defined? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010 to FR-013]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK007 Do the username, sign-in, and password-change requirements align without contradictory statements about whether a current password is always required? [Consistency, Spec §User Story 2, Spec §FR-009 to FR-013]
- [ ] CHK008 Are the role and identity requirements consistent across account creation, sign-in, and password updates, including a single role value and unique username identity? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, FR-020, FR-022]
- [ ] CHK009 Do the audit, session invalidation, and rate-limit requirements align with the stated security posture without conflicting with the authentication flow? [Consistency, Spec §FR-016 to FR-024]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK010 Are the success criteria measurable enough to verify outcomes such as update success, rejection cases, and audit trail coverage? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-001 to SC-008]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the definition of success for the authentication and password-change API flow specific enough to support review and validation without implementation detail? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §User Story 3, Spec §FR-025 to FR-029]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK012 Are primary, alternate, exception, and recovery scenarios all represented for the login and password-change user journeys? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 1-3, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK013 Are zero-state and boundary scenarios defined for invalid credentials, blank input, duplicate usernames, and maximum rate-limit behavior? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, Spec §FR-002, FR-023]
- [ ] CHK014 Are assumptions and dependencies around data persistence, session invalidation, and audit logging explicitly documented so reviewers can assess missing coverage? [Assumption, Spec §Key Entities, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- This checklist evaluates the quality of the written requirements, not the implementation outcome.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
